nodes.name: Writer Trigger
nodes.notes: The shared writer of Enrich Contacts (2026-09-09). One item: { base, peopleTableId, peopleFields, contactSourceMulti, dncDomains, provider, companies:[{recordId, domain, cap}], people:{domain:[...]} }. Reads what People already holds at these domains, merges one provider's chunk into it (held rows filled, never overwritten, first writer wins because the lanes run in priority order), cleans, drops DNC, PATCHes in tens. Answers counters only.

nodes.name: Read Held
nodes.notes: What People already holds at this chunk's domains, one call per 100 domains, with the fill fields. Domain on People is a lookup through the Companies link; the {Domain} filter matches its text.

nodes.name: Any People?
nodes.notes: Merge People answers one {_empty} item when the chunk brought nothing new and nothing to fill.

nodes.name: Write People
nodes.notes: The one People writer: PATCH /v0/{base}/{People} with {performUpsert: {fieldsToMergeOn: ["Contact Key"]}, records (ten per request, held rows carry their id), typecast: true}, 200 ms apart, so 50 rows per second. The upsert is idempotent, so a request that never got an answer (connection aborted: the box dropping sockets under load, 13,907 rows lost on CaaB 2026-09-09) is retried up to three times, 3 s apart. A 429 is not an error here (neverError) and is never retried: it locks the base for 30 s. Written rows are counted from the answer records[].
